children: Keppel Ltd.'s deal to sell its telecommunications unit M1 to telecom peer StarHub through an all-share transaction is the most optimal outcome the asset manager could have achieved, says Citi analyst Brandon Lee in a note. The deal--which requires Keppel to retain its StarHub shares for a 12-month period--delays Keppel's full exit from M1 until at least 1H 2028, he notes. However, the Singapore telecom market has only around four major companies and a previous deal with another buyer had to be terminated, he says. He reckons Keppel could eventually sell its StarHub stake via a block trade, given its strong limited-partner network. Citi retains its buy rating and its 14.46 Singapore dollar target price. The stock is up 0.4% at S$8.35.(megan.cheah@wsj.com)
